Follow [execute a handoff](course/execute.qmd) for the preparation-to-return procedure. This page owns profile/resource and identity requirements.

SCGSim prepares portable handoffs; the caller owns where and how a prepared
solver runs. A profile records the launch shape and the resources supplied by
the caller. It does not submit a scheduler job or open a native desktop.

## Fixed handoff profiles

Profile names describe launch shape, not a site or hostname.

| Profile | Intended use | Recorded evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `direct-local` | Run the generated Palace shell script on one host | Executable, inputs, environment, exit state, and artifacts |
| `slurm-single-node` | Submit the generated Palace batch script for one node | Job identity, requested resources, launch shape, and artifacts |
| `slurm-multi-node` | Submit the generated Palace batch script for multiple nodes | Job identity, node/resource request, launch shape, and artifacts |

The Palace caller supplies a non-empty resource mapping. Slurm profiles
require `ntasks`, `cpus_per_task`, and `nodes`. `slurm-single-node` requires
one node; `slurm-multi-node` requires at least two and a `mem` or
`mem_per_cpu` request. Resource sizing is the caller's responsibility. Slurm
allocation keys such as `ntasks`, `cpus_per_task`, `nodes`, and `mem` become
`#SBATCH` directives. Scheduler output and error logs remain bound to the
handoff's Palace log. The caller also supplies the executable, any host setup
commands, and optional launcher tokens. None of these values is a SCGSim
site-wide default.

## Palace command shapes

The generated command depends on the profile and `resources.command_style`:

| Selection | Generated launch behavior |
|---|---|
| `direct-local` + `binary` | Calls the configured executable with `config.json`; `threads` sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS`. SCGSim adds no MPI launcher or rank argument, so use this only when direct invocation matches the host's Palace build. |
| `direct-local` + `wrapper` | Calls the configured Palace MPI wrapper with `-np <processes> -nt <threads> config.json`. The installed `palace` script wraps an MPI launcher (by default `mpirun`) and accepts these controls; see the [Palace runner guide](https://awslabs.github.io/palace/stable/run/) and [parallelism guide](https://awslabs.github.io/palace/stable/guide/parallelism/). |
| Either Slurm profile | Writes `run_palace.sbatch` with the caller's scheduler resources and invokes the configured launcher (default `srun`) before the Palace executable and `config.json`. Slurm profiles require `command_style="binary"`; wrapper mode is rejected. |

For Slurm, the user submits the prepared script with `sbatch`; the script's
default `srun` launches the Palace binary inside the allocation. `srun` is the
scheduler launcher, not the Palace MPI wrapper. Do not stack the Palace
`-np`/`-nt` wrapper on top of the Slurm launcher. The required
`cpus_per_task` sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS` unless the caller separately supplies a
`threads` value; keep an override aligned with the scheduler allocation. The
configured executable, launcher, and site setup commands must match the
target host. SCGSim does not guess an MPI setup.

The Palace script performs a native `--dry-run` compatibility check on the
exact handoff `config.json` before the solve command. A failed check records a
preflight failure and does not invoke the solver. Successful preparation alone
does not establish that the executable, config, or native geometry is valid.

## Handoff lifecycle

```text
configure model -> inspect input summary -> prepare handoff
-> transfer the complete package -> run on the target host
-> retrieve the complete returned package -> resolve and show results
```

For Palace, retain `handoff.handoff_id` in preparation-side notes outside the
transferred package. After the full returned run directory is retrieved,
`resolve_palace_result(run_dir, expected_handoff_id=...)` checks it against
that independently retained identity before showing results. Do not learn the
expected identity from files that arrived with the returned package.

For AEDT, transfer the prepared run directory to the AEDT host and retrieve
the complete returned run directory. `resolve_results(run_dir)` verifies the
receipt-bound artifacts; `ResolvedRun.show_all_results()` displays the
verified primary, benchmark, and requested EPR evidence. Copying only an EPR
JSON file is not a substitute for resolving the returned package.

External gdsfactory/cloud execution is unsupported and is never a fallback.
Preparation does not silently submit a scheduler job or open AEDT. The
[Palace tutorial](tutorial-xmon-palace.qmd) and [AEDT tutorial](tutorial-xmon-aedt.qmd)
show their backend-specific handoff and return steps.
